You are implementing the "feedback de una sesión" change in kurasu (`app/`), in a git worktree on branch `feat/feedback-de-sesion`. Work with high reasoning effort. Your current directory is that worktree; do not touch the main checkout at /home/agus/workspace/filadd/agentic-engineering-famaf-extension-course except to read the scratch files named below.

## The change

Read these before touching code:
- `app/docs/architecture/feedback-de-sesion.md` (in your worktree), and the notes it links: `modelo-de-datos.md`, `estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md`, `acceso-a-datos.md`, `carga-y-acciones-de-la-web.md`.
- The program design: /home/agus/workspace/filadd/agentic-engineering-famaf-extension-course/.scratch/feedback-de-sesion/program-design/kurasu.md. Its six branches name every type, function, component and file the change adds or touches. Follow it.
- The design tree: /home/agus/workspace/filadd/agentic-engineering-famaf-extension-course/.scratch/feedback-de-sesion/design.md.
- The prototypes, which settle how the screens look and behave, not how they are coded: `app/docs/prototipos/feedback-sesion.html` (student) and `app/docs/prototipos/admin-feedback.html` (teacher).

Summary. Feedback is a new poll type, `"feedback"`, in the existing `polls` table, with no migration. A student answers with a score from 1 to 5, picked from five emojis, plus optional free text, and can change the answer while the poll is active. The response value is `{ pick: 1..5, text?: string }`; a present `text` that is blank (empty, only spaces or only line breaks) is rejected with 400 by the contract schema, the web never sends it, and a text with content is stored as is, spaces included; `Polls.vote` no longer strips text. Students never get results for a feedback poll (`results: null`, active or closed). The teacher sees five bars (one count per score) in `PollResults.feedback`, and the list of responses with each student's name and avatar in `AdminPoll.responses` (`FeedbackResponse { id, user { id, name, avatar }, pick, text? }`, ordered by response id), present only on feedback polls, read in one query for all feedback polls by `ResponsesStore.feedbackOf`. The count query groups feedback by pick without reading the text. There is no endpoint of its own for the list. On the web: `VoteForm` hands feedback polls to `FeedbackForm` (local state `isEditing`), with `FeedbackScale`, `FeedbackAnswer` (with an `<action>` slot) and `feedback-faces.ts`; the error is inline with no toast; `PollCard` uses the `chat-messages` icon; `pollMeta` and `ClosedPolls` handle feedback; the teacher side adds Feedback to `NewPollMenu`, a feedback branch in `PollResults` and `PollPreview`, a `<leading>` slot in `PollActions`, and `FeedbackResponsesButton`, `FeedbackResponsesSheet` and `FeedbackResponseRow`. Out of scope: anything not in the program design, any change to other poll types beyond what the regression rows below cover.

## The tasks

They live in Entire trail #1 (https://entire.com/gh/filadd/-/trails/1). Work them in this order:
1. **El tipo feedback en el contrato.** `PollType` adds `"feedback"`. `ResponseValue` adds `{pick 1..5, text?}`, with the non-blank check on `text`. `PollResults.feedback` adds the five counts. `FeedbackResponse` and `AdminPoll.responses` go in `contract/src/polls.ts`.
2. **El alumno responde un feedback (API).** `fitsPoll` adds the feedback branch. `forStudent` returns `results: null` for feedback. The upsert keeps the response id and `Polls.vote` stops stripping empty text.
3. **El profe ve el resumen y la lista (API).** `counts` groups the picks without reading the text and `tally` adds the feedback branch. `ResponsesStore.feedbackOf` reads responses with name and avatar in one query, and `forTeacher` puts them in `AdminPoll.responses`. Adds the feedback session to `fixtures/polls.sql`.
4. **La tarjeta del alumno (web).** `FeedbackForm` with `isEditing`, `FeedbackScale`, `FeedbackAnswer`, `feedback-faces.ts`. Also the `PollCard` icon, `pollMeta`, `ClosedPolls` and `useVote` (no toast). The closed-poll message in `ActivePolls` becomes "El profe cerró esa encuesta antes de que respondieras." for every type.
5. **La tarjeta del profe (web).** `NewPollMenu` adds Feedback, `PollResults` the feedback branch, `PollActions` the `<leading>` slot. Adds `FeedbackResponsesButton`, `FeedbackResponsesSheet` (with "Todavía no hay respuestas." when empty) and `FeedbackResponseRow`. `PollPreview` draws a feedback draft as the student sees it, disabled.

Test fixtures that go with the tasks: `apps/api/test/fixtures/polls.sql` gets the feedback polls and their responses in a session of their own, with students of known name and avatar (A19 checks that the teacher's list of the session with the other polls names no student); `apps/web/test/fixtures/content.ts` and `helpers/poll-store.ts` get a sample feedback poll for the student and one for the teacher with `responses`, and `pollStore` creates a feedback draft with `results.feedback` at zero and `responses: []`.

## Tracker states

The tracker is the description of Entire trail #1, a markdown checklist (see `.mahou/implement.md`). There is no in-progress state. When a task is implemented, tested and committed, read the description with `entire trail show 1 --json`, change that task's `- [ ]` to `- [x]`, and write the whole description back with `entire trail update 1 --body "<full body>"` (it replaces the description entirely). Work the trail does not list becomes a new `- [ ]` line, worked like the rest; a task that dissolves is struck with a line saying why. Name each in your report. Do not run `entire trail link` or anything that pushes.

## The tests

The rows below are copied from /home/agus/workspace/filadd/agentic-engineering-famaf-extension-course/.scratch/feedback-de-sesion/test-design/kurasu.md. On `test` rows (including `test + manual`): a `★` row is a new test you write, at the integration level the repository uses (`apps/api/test`, `apps/web/test`), named after what the test proves; an unstarred row whose expected outcome is the one the suite already checks is a regression row, left untouched and still passing; an unstarred row whose expected outcome changed is updated to match it; a test listed under `Deleted:` is removed. Row ids are for the matrix only: no row id, tracker id or scratch path in any test name, comment or docstring. The `manual` part of a row is for later; do not run it.

- `ResponseValue`, `PollResults`, `FeedbackResponse` y `AdminPoll.responses` (`packages/contract/src/polls.ts`): schemas compartidos; se prueban por los endpoints de `A` y por las pantallas de `B`. La regla `test-location` solo permite tests en `apps/api/test` y `apps/web/test`.

## Lo que el diseño deja para el programa

- Dónde se arma el batch y cómo devuelve las encuestas que cierra.
- Qué error responde cada rechazo nuevo.
- Dónde vive el control de la destacada para no repetirlo en cada escritura.
- Cómo la web cuenta los efectos para las confirmaciones.
- Qué acciones del profe pierden el parche optimista.
- En qué componentes entran el panel de preguntas, el modal y las confirmaciones.
- Cómo se reparte el cálculo del camino entre el inicio y el admin.

## Decisiones de esta etapa

- **Q1 · NotFeatured**: un error nuevo, 409, para activar una encuesta o prender las preguntas destacadas fuera de la destacada. Las escrituras del estudiante no lo usan: conservan el 404 que ya devuelven para una sesión que no pueden tocar, así el estudiante no distingue una sesión vieja de una que no existe. La web no deja hacer ninguna de estas acciones fuera de la destacada, así que el rechazo solo llega con una pantalla vieja (el usuario aceptó la propuesta).
- **Q2 · El servicio arma el batch (C2)**: `Sessions.update` coordina el cambio de destacada. Pide a `SessionsStore`, `PollsStore` y `HandsStore` sus escrituras sin ejecutarlas, con `writes`, y las corre juntas con el puerto `Batch`. `writes` es la versión diferida de los métodos de escritura de `Repository`, y `repositoryOf` la arma desde las `statements` que ya tiene, así que todos los stores la heredan sin código propio. Se descartó `SessionsStore.changeFeatured`, que seguía el patrón de `MaterialsStore` (un store que escribe en tablas de otros), y un método `Write` por caso en cada store.
- **Avisos al aula**: la sesión que sale recibe `session`, `polls` y `hands`, porque el profe puede tener abierta su página en otra pestaña y las listas de su admin cambian.
- **El nodo del camino**: el inicio y el admin usan la misma regla, y por eso el cálculo vive en `rail-look.ts`. Los dos dibujan lo mismo en cada nodo: check en `done`, estrella en `live`, nada en `later`; el admin suma `locked`, vacío y punteado, para las deshabilitadas.
- **La destacada se busca una vez** (pedido del usuario): `ContentTab` la toma con `useFeaturedSession`, un `select` sobre la lista del admin, y se la pasa a los dos switches con la sesión de la página. La sesión de la página ya dice si es la destacada (`session.featured`); la lista hace falta para saber cuál es la otra.
- **Sin números en el admin** (pedido del usuario sobre el mockup de la lista): la lista del admin marca la destacada con la estrella en su nodo y no con un chip, y ningún nodo lleva número. Sin números, "Sesión N de M" deja de tener sentido: sale de la card de arriba y de la card de Contenido, y los diálogos nombran a la otra destacada por su título.
- **Q3 · Todas las sesiones**: la lista del inicio ya tiene a la destacada (prototipo), así que se titula "Todas las sesiones" con o sin destacada, como en el admin. El nodo de la destacada pierde el número y lleva una estrella, la del chip "Destacada". Los componentes del inicio y del admin toman el nombre de la marca: `FeaturedSession`, `AllSessions`, `AdminFeatured`.

## Cambios a la fuente

Lo que este program design decidió distinto de `../design.md` y de las notas en `2e23169`. Se registra al final, con `mahou:write-documentation`.

- **Q3**: la lista del inicio se titula "Todas las sesiones" e incluye a la destacada, cuyo nodo lleva una estrella sin número. La rama 7 de `design.md`, la sección 🏠 Inicio del estudiante de `estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md` (que dice "Otras sesiones" y "Sesiones", "todas las demás habilitadas") y el prototipo `inicio-responsive.html` dicen otra cosa. `novedades-por-mail.md` dice "entre las otras sesiones" en dos lugares.
- **Sin números ni chip en el admin**: la sección 🛠️ Admin de las sesiones de `estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md` dice que el número de una sesión es su posición y que la destacada lleva el chip "Destacada"; los prototipos `admin-sesiones.html` y `admin-sesion.html` muestran el chip, los números, "Sesión N de M" y "la sesión 3" en los diálogos; la rama 7 de `design.md` nombra el chip.
- **El link `?sesion=<id>` de la destacada**: como la lista ahora incluye a la destacada, el link con su id despliega su card en la lista. La sección 🏠 de `estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md` dice que el id de la destacada se ve como sin el parámetro, y el warning de `novedades-por-mail.md` dice que ese link "no abre nada más". El mail sigue mandando la home sin parámetro para la destacada, así que esto solo cambia un link viejo cuya sesión pasó a ser la destacada.
- **Quién arma el batch (Q2)**: la tabla de `acceso-a-datos.md` pone el cambio de destacada en la fila de sesiones, como una operación del store de sesiones. Ahora lo arma el servicio de sesiones con escrituras sin ejecutar de tres stores y un puerto de batch. La sección ✍️ Escrituras y batches ya dice que cada escritura existe como sentencia sin ejecutar; falta decir que el core las pide así y las corre juntas.
- **Q1**: `invariantes.md` y la nota de estados no dicen qué responde un rechazo. Activar una encuesta o prender las preguntas destacadas fuera de la destacada responde `NotFeatured`; las escrituras del estudiante, el 404 de hoy. Va en la sección de reglas de la API de la nota de estados.

---

---
name: delegate
description: Delegate work by spawning another agent as a herdr tab.
---
# The herdr-subagents protocol

What you follow as a parent agent driving herdr subagents. You drive every exchange: you prompt, your children reply.

## Your prompts — `<supervisor-agent>`

Wrap every prompt you send to a child in `<supervisor-agent>…</supervisor-agent>`. The tag is how the child tells your directive from a human steering it directly — an untagged message reaching the child means a human has taken over that tab.

## Your child's questions — `<subagent-ask>`

A child that needs a decision ends its turn with the question wrapped in `<subagent-ask>…</subagent-ask>`. When you collect, that tag is your discriminator: present means the child is asking you something (reply, and do not close the tab); absent means the message is the child's result.

## Invoking delegation

The delegate skill is invoked as `/skill:delegate` on pi and `/delegate` on claude. A child invokes it on its own harness. If you direct a cross-harness child to delegate, name the form for its harness in your prompt.

When a message carries a skill invocation (any `/skill:...` or `/...` command), it comes **first, outside the `<supervisor-agent>` tag** — it is a harness command, not part of the tagged payload. The command and the opening tag share the first line, space-separated: `/skill:implement <supervisor-agent>...`. This holds for every skill, not only delegation: a parent directing a child to run `/skill:implement`, `/skill:tdd`, or any other skill prefixes the command before the tag on the same line.

---

# Delegate

You drive subagents through a single interface that wraps herdr. It handles the fragile parts — verifying the spawn landed, confirming the prompt was delivered, tracking pane and tab ids — so you treat each command as trustworthy and act on what it reports.

Use the `subagent` tool for all delegation commands. Pass `command` and the relevant `options`:

| command  | options                                           |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| spawn    | `{ kind, agent?, label, model?, body?, body_file?, worktree?, branch?, base? }` |
| prompt   | `{ pane_id, body | body_file }`                               |
| wait     | `{ pane_id, timeout? }`                           |
| collect  | `{ pane_id }`                                     |
| close    | `{ tab_id }`                                      |
| list     | `{}`                                              |
| read     | `{ pane_id, lines? }`                             |
| unblock  | `{ pane_id, keys }`                               |

`wait` is rarely needed — your session auto-wakes you when a child finishes.

All children are herdr tabs. One tab, one task. A child lives in your workspace unless you give it a worktree, which puts it in a workspace of its own.

## When to delegate

Delegate when the work is genuinely separable and worth a tab of its own. Prefer breadth — several children at your own level — over deep chains. Close your children before spawning the next batch.

Label each tab after the work it is doing; a workspace of labelled tabs is your fleet view.

## Spawn

- `kind` is required and never self-detected. Your default is your own harness; pass the other only when the work or the caller explicitly asks for it. Only `pi` and `claude` are supported.
- `agent` is optional. Omit it to dispatch a generic child running the harness's default agent (it still receives the herdr onboarding). When given, it is a name defined in the project's agent files, never a path — and the name is all you provide: the child's system prompt is applied from the definition at spawn, so never paste the definition into the prompt nor direct the child to read it.
- `model` is optional. Omitted, the child runs its harness's default model. It is a model name of the child's harness, passed through verbatim, so what is valid depends on `kind`. A bare id that more than one provider carries is ambiguous — pi exits on it and the spawn fails — so qualify it with the provider, such as `zai/glm-5.3-flash`. When you spawn without a model named by the work or the caller, pick one yourself: judge the task's difficulty and choose the cheapest model available that can solve it. Reach for a heavier model only when the work needs the capability — mechanical tasks never do.
- `body` is optional. Given, the task is delivered with the spawn — one call instead of spawn-then-prompt. Wrap it in `<supervisor-agent>…</supervisor-agent>` exactly as you would with `prompt`; delivery is verified the same way. Every message after it goes through `prompt`. Pass it as text, or through `body_file` with a path to a file whose content is exactly the body (absolute, or relative to the cwd).
- The label is final; a child never renames its own tab.

Returns the new child's `pane_id` and `tab_id`. Keep both — you prompt and collect by `pane_id`, and close by `tab_id`. If spawn fails, the half-created tab is closed and the failure is reported; surface that to the human rather than retrying blindly. Two failures are different: `blocked` means the child came up on a startup dialog and never became ready. It is alive, so its tab is kept and its pane comes back with the dialog on it — see **Blocked children**. And a spawn with `body` can fail at delivery: the child is alive and tracked, and the failure names its `pane_id` — retry with `prompt`.

## Worktrees

`worktree` gives a child its own checkout on its own branch, in its own herdr workspace, instead of sharing your working directory.

Use it when the child will **write** — implementing, refactoring, fixing a bug — and above all when several children write at once. Sharing one checkout means they overwrite each other's edits and fight over the same branch.

It is not the default. Research, planning, design, review — anything answered by reading — belongs in your own checkout, where the child sees the code you actually have and leaves nothing behind. A single child making changes is usually fine without one too; isolation pays off when there is something to isolate from.

- `branch` names the branch. A new name creates a worktree; an existing one joins it.
- `base` is what a new branch forks from. Omitted, your current HEAD.
- Nothing else changes. You prompt, collect, and close a worktree child exactly like any other.

Several children can share one worktree. Point a second child at an existing branch and it lands in the same checkout alongside the first — that is how you put a reviewer on another child's work, or hand a branch from one child to the next. Children sharing a checkout see each other's edits, so give them non-overlapping work, or run them one after another.

Close children as you always do. A worktree outlives its children until the last one goes, and closing that last child takes the checkout with it — so a sibling still working there is never disturbed. The branch always survives: name it when you report a child's result, or the work is lost to whoever reads the report.

Uncommitted changes are never discarded. If the last child's checkout is dirty, the close reports that and the child stays open — prompt it to commit, then close it again.

## Prompt

Wrap **every** prompt you send to a child in `<supervisor-agent>…</supervisor-agent>`. Tagging is what tells the child it is a supervisor directive rather than a human steering it. The first prompt can ride `spawn`'s `body`; `prompt` is for every message after it. Either takes the body as text or through a file path (`body_file`); the file's content is exactly the body, tag included.

Delivery is verified: the interface watches for the child to act on the prompt and resends if the first send is dropped. A child that is already `working` receives the prompt as a steer — no state change follows a steer, so the accepted submission itself is the receipt and the message is never resent.

When a child needs you, your session wakes you automatically, so you never arm a wake yourself: a finished turn (`done`, or an `idle` that ends a turn) wakes you to collect, `blocked` wakes you to surface the dialog to the human, the resume from a block wakes you so you know they answered, and a lost child (`gone`) wakes you too.

## Blocked children

`blocked` is herdr recognising a dialog on a child's screen — a tool approval, a question it opened instead of asking you, a startup trust prompt. It is neither terminal nor a failure: the child is alive and one keypress from carrying on. It is also the state most in need of you, because unlike a finished turn it will never resolve on its own.

A blocked child wakes you. What you do with it:

- `read` its pane to see what is being asked. This is the one screen read in the interface; it is for a blocked child, not for checking progress.
- **Tell the human what it needs and which tab to answer it in** — name the tab label and the pane id. The answer is theirs to give, not yours: you cannot know whether a permission prompt should be granted, and a question the child asked is a question for a person.
- You are woken again when the child resumes, so you can carry on without watching the tab.

`unblock` sends key presses (`enter`, `esc`, `1 enter`) and reports whether the block cleared. Use it **only when the human has explicitly told you to answer that dialog** — "yes, accept it" is your authorization, and it saves them a tab switch. Never on your own judgement, and never as a way to keep a child moving. It refuses a child that is not blocked: keys sent to an idle child are typed into its prompt box and corrupt its next prompt.

A child that asks through a dialog rather than `<subagent-ask>` has misrouted its question — surface it, and prompt it to use the tag next time. Whoever answers a dialog, the child cannot tell you from the human.

## Collect

When a child finishes, you are woken to collect it.

Returns `{pane_id, label, agent, status, message?, error?}`. `status` reflects herdr's state, **not** task success — a child that gives up still reaches `done`. Read `message` and judge the result yourself.

The `<subagent-ask>…</subagent-ask>` tag in the child's final message marks a question for you rather than a result.

`blocked` is non-terminal: the child is waiting, not finished. See **Blocked children**.

Once you no longer need a child, you can close it.

## Close

Close a child once you have its result and no longer need it. Closing before spawning the next batch keeps the fleet clean. The timing is a delegation question, not a results question: keep a child open because a fix round is coming, close it when nothing more will be delegated to it.

## The fleet

Run `list` to see every tracked child and its status. A wake can be missed; `list` is the durable backstop you run on demand, so a missed wake is never fatal. Run it whenever you are unsure what is outstanding.

A child that stalls has no automatic timeout. Surface it to the human as a fleet item — do not kill it.

## Inspection (discouraged)

The interface is your complete surface. If it reports something you cannot act on, surface the pane to the human rather than reaching past it.

## Nesting

A child you spawn can delegate further by invoking the delegate skill on its own harness; nesting works to any depth. The judgement above — breadth over chains, close before the next batch — applies at every level.


## Agent definitions on pi

The `agent` option of `spawn` takes the name of an agent definition — a `.md` file under the project's `.pi/agents/`, scanned recursively. Run `ls -R .pi/agents` to see which names exist before picking one. The name is all you pass: the child's system prompt is applied from the definition automatically, so never paste the definition into the body nor tell the child to read the file. If `.pi/agents` does not exist, the project defines no agents — omit `agent` rather than looking elsewhere.

Resume an agent session for a trail.

The trail may be given as the first argument or via --trail, as a project number,
ID, or <repo>/<number>. Without one, the current branch's parent is used. --branch selects its
working branch in this repository. Multiple matches require an explicit branch.

sessions on the trail branch, and ask whether Entire should start the agent. If

the latest checkpoint on the trail branch. Use --session or --checkpoint to
resume an exact session or checkpoint.

anything out.

Subagent impl kurasu (w45:p2, done):
Branch `feat/preguntas-en-la-card`: all nine tasks are implemented, tested and committed, and `pnpm run check` and `pnpm test` pass. I did not touch A45 beyond writing the migration, and nothing was run for the `manual` parts.

## Commits

- `613b8a6` feat(api): mark the featured session and move it with one batch
- `3482133` feat(api): let students write only in the featured session
- `0aa9de9` feat(web): show the featured session on the student home and list all sessions
- `5a82327` feat(web): ask and vote on questions from the featured card
- `1e37216` feat(web): feature and enable sessions from the session admin
- `dc61641` feat(web): mark the featured session with a star on the teacher's list
- `8dd0fe6` feat(web): activate polls only in the featured session and switch its questions on
- `5f0b8e9` docs(web): say featured in the student questions comment

The first commit attempt was rejected by the lefthook `check` (lint). I fixed the lint errors and committed again; nothing was skipped.

## Tasks

1. **Mark and contract.** The migration is `0004_featured_session`, with the two boolean columns and a partial unique index on `featured`.
   - `SessionSummary` and `SessionChange` have the new fields.
   - `NotFeatured` (409) exists, and `questions-opened` has its label, line and `bg-rose`.
   - `PATCH /admin/sessions/:id` declares `SessionDisabled` and `NotFeatured`; `PATCH /admin/polls/:id` declares `NotFeatured`.
2. **Batches.** `Write` and `Batch` are in `core/src/batch.ts`, and `Repository` has `writes`. `repositoryOf` builds `writes` from its `statements`, `D1Batch` implements the port, and `worker.ts` wires it.
3. **Changing the featured session.** `Sessions.update` follows the design.
   - The batch order is: unmark and turn off the leaving session, close its active polls (omitted when there are none), lower its hands, apply the change.
   - Afterwards it drops `questions-opened` and the closed polls' `poll-opened`, notifies `session`, `polls` and `hands`, and handles `questions-opened` on and off.
   - `Sessions.featured` reads the mark. A change with no leaving session uses the plain `store.update`.
4. **Write rule.** `featuredSession` replaces `visibleSession` in student writes. Activating outside the featured session answers `NotFeatured`, and the first vote keeps `poll-opened`.
5. **Student home.** `FeaturedSession`, `AllSessions`, `railLook`, the star icon, `RailNode` `later` and `SessionLinks` `featured` are in. Active polls are asked for per featured session, and `/aula` takes the mark.
6. **Questions panel.** `FeaturedQuestions` goes in the `questions` slot, and `QuestionList` takes `emptyText`.
7. **Session admin.**
   - New components: `FeaturedSwitch`, `EnableSessionDialog`, `FeaturedEffects` and `useFeaturedSession`. `ConfirmDialog` and `ConfirmAction` gain `content` and `confirmIcon`.
   - `EnabledSwitch` opens the modal when enabling and asks before disabling the featured session.
   - `useUpdateSession` patches only `featuredQuestions` and disabling a non-featured session, and invalidates the five keys.
   - "Sesión N de M" is gone.
   - `useApiQuery` and `useAdminSessions` gained a third type parameter so `select` types.
8. **Teacher list.** `AdminFeatured`, `AdminSessionRail` with `railLook`, the star, dashed nodes for disabled sessions and no numbers or chip. The "Ninguna sesión destacada" note is in place.
9. **Teacher classroom.** `PollStateActions` takes `isFeatured`, and `AdminPollsTab` and `AdminPanelPolls` show the "Solo se activan encuestas…" note under drafts. `FeaturedQuestionsSwitch` sits above the questions list.

Subagent validate kurasu (w45:p3, done):
## Validación manual: preguntas en la card destacada

I ran all 27 manual rows against the local stack. 25 passed on the first run, 2 passed after a fix, and none are blocked. I found no bugs outside the rows. The fixes are committed on `feat/preguntas-en-la-card` and not pushed.

**Report:** `/home/agus/workspace/filadd/agentic-engineering-famaf-extension-course/.scratch/preguntas-en-la-card/reports/validate/index.html`, with `api-evidence.txt` and the screenshots in `shots/` next to it.

### Results

| Rows | Result |
|---|---|
| A1, A2, A3, A5, A8, A10, A14, A17, A18, A27, A28, A35, A45 | pass |
| B2, B5, B12, B13, B15, B21, B23, B29, B31, B33, B36, B41 | pass |
| B24 | fixed, `19360f3` |
| B39 | fixed, `ee83edd` |

- **API rows:** I called the API over HTTP through the Vite `/api` proxy and checked the lists, polls, raised hands and changelog. I watched the classroom notices with a WebSocket client connected as a student and as the teacher.
- **A45:** the worktree had no local data, so I copied the main checkout's `apps/infra/.alchemy` into it: 24 sessions, with migrations 0001–0003 applied. Starting the stack applied `0004_featured_session`, and every session came out with both columns false. On a copy of that database, marking a second session as featured failed with `UNIQUE constraint failed: sessions.featured`.
- **B33:** the confirmation can only fail if the request fails. I aborted the PATCH with an agent-browser route, which is a network failure, not a 500 from the server.
- **B41:** with 3 s of added latency, the switch was already on 0.4 s after the click.

### Fixes

- **B24, `fix(web): color the enable dialog's featured warning as in the prototype` (`19360f3`):**
  - **What failed:** the text and the counts in the enable dialog's warning were right, but the box was peach with dark text. `admin-sesion.html` draws it pink (`#F9DDE1`) with dark red text (`#8A2E3D`).
  - **Change:** `EnableSessionDialog.tsx` now uses those two colours. I re-ran the row: the warning matches the prototype and the request is `{"enabled":true,"featured":true}`.
  - **Test:** none added, because B24 is a `test + manual` row and the existing test checks the content, not the colour.
- **B39, `fix(web): show the not-featured note under the last draft in the polls tab` (`ee83edd`):**
  - **What failed:** in the Encuestas tab of a session that is not the featured one, the line "Solo se activan encuestas en la sesión destacada." came after the whole list, below the closed polls. The row, the program design (7.1) and the prototype put it under the last draft.
  - **Change:** `AdminPollsTab.tsx` now renders the line right after the last draft. The classroom panel (`AdminPanelPolls`) already placed it there, because its closed polls sit in a separate folded section.
  - **Test:** new test "outside the featured session the note sits under the last draft, above the closed polls" in `apps/web/test/admin-polls.test.tsx`. It fails without the fix and passes with it.

### Check and tests after the fixes

`pnpm run check`:
```
 Tasks:    7 successful, 7 total
$ tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json
$ oxlint && oxfmt --check .
All matched files use the correct format.
Finished in 206ms on 492 files using 16 threads.
```
`pnpm --filter @kurasu/web test` (both fixes are web-only, so I did not re-run the API suite):
```
 Test Files  25 passed (25)
      Tests  285 passed (285)
```
The lefthook check passed again on both commits.

### Left behind

- **Inside the worktree:** `app/apps/infra/.alchemy/`, the copy of the local data, which git ignores. I changed it during the run:
  - It now has migration 0004 applied.
  - It holds the six "PC …" sessions I created, with their polls, questions and raised hands.
  - "PC B24 habilitar con otra" is the featured session.
  - I disabled the 18 "Val …" sessions during the run and enabled them all again afterwards.

  The main checkout's `.alchemy` was not touched.
- **Outside the worktree:**
  - `/tmp/kurasu-val/`: scripts, cookie jars for the test users, HAR captures, `ids.env`, and a stray `B2-01-card.png`.
  - `/tmp/kurasu-a45/db.sqlite`: the database copy from A45.
  - The report folder above.
  - A new `reports/validate/` line in the scratch folder's `status.md`.
- **Processes and browsers:** I stopped the stack and every WebSocket listener, and nothing is listening on ports 1337 or 5173. I closed the agent-browser sessions `pc-val-student`, `pc-val-teacher` and `pc-val-proto`.
- **Git stash:** I used one temporary stash entry, `pc-val-b39-check`, to run the new test without the fix. I applied it back and dropped it.
- **Auto-mode:** it blocked two tool calls when its classifier timed out. Neither ran, and I repeated both without changes.

Subagent review kurasu (w45:p4, done):
# Agentic review report: kurasu (`app/`)

All three rounds ran: 26 fixes and 18 skips. The fixes are committed in eight commits on `feat/preguntas-en-la-card`, nothing is pushed, and `pnpm run check` and `pnpm test` pass. None of the fixes changes how the app looks or behaves.

The changeset was the branch measured against `d09d518` (`git diff d09d518...HEAD`), plus each round's uncommitted fixes. The ledger is at `/home/agus/workspace/filadd/agentic-engineering-famaf-extension-course/.scratch/preguntas-en-la-card/reports/review/ledger.md`.

**Reviewers.** Each round had 14 fresh reviewers on Sonnet 5.5:
- four facets: reuse, simplification, efficiency, altitude;
- one conventions reviewer per source: `app/AGENTS.md`, your style file, the local wiki entries `architecture`, `api`, `web`, `fence` and `alchemy/local-tests`, and the global entries `naming/booleans`, `react/component-modules` and `tanstack-query/operation-hooks`.

The auto-mode classifier rate-limited (429) a few spawns and one batch read. Each was retried and ran, and no reviewer was skipped.

**Rounds.**

| Round | Findings | Fixes | Skips |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 46 | 15 | 11 |
| 2 | 12 | 7 | 2 |
| 3 | 9 | 4 | 5 |

The review stopped at round 3, the skill's limit, not because the reviewers ran out of findings.

## Fixes and their commits

**`044a280` refactor(api): run the featured session's leaving in one helper and name the deferred writes once**
- **1, 16, 17.** `Sessions.update` checked `Option.isSome(leaving)` three times, read the featured session on every update, and did a second `store.get` on the plain path. Now:
  - one `updateLeaving` helper holds the whole leaving path, and its read-back uses `existingSession`;
  - `featured()` runs only when `change.featured === true`;
  - the plain path uses the row `store.update` returns, as the base did;
  - `leavingOf` returns only the id.
- **2.** The `Writes` comment had pushed the `Repository` doc comment off its type; each type has its own comment again.
- **3.** `repositoryOf` returned the same object as both `statements` and `writes`. It is now only `writes`, and `codes`, `materials` and `users` use that name.
- **4.** `polls.isFeatured` re-read the session itself; it is now built on `featuredSession`.
- **14 (part).** Removed the narrative comment above `leavingOf` and rewrapped the long `Sessions` comment.

**`5eddd62` test(api): raise the hand each raised-hands test lowers**
- **22.** Ana's seeded hand made "raising the hand…" pass whether or not the request created a hand, and the lowering test depended on what earlier tests left. The fixture drops that hand, and the lowering test raises the hand it lowers.

**`253abbe` refactor(web): draw the session rail node in one component**
- **5, 18.** Both rails drew the same check and star node. That is now one `SessionRailNode`. The look names are listed once, in `RailNodeLook`, and `RailLook` is derived from it.

**`1b5d4d3` refactor(web): share the switch button, row class, error text and warning colours of the session switches**
- **6.** The four new switch buttons share `ui/SwitchButton`.
- **7.** `FeaturedSwitch` picks its confirmation once with `confirmationOf`, instead of three overlapping branches.
- **11.** The warning's hex colours are now the theme colours `blush` and `wine`, with the same values.
- **12.** `EnabledSwitch` and `EnableSessionDialog` are an `EnabledSwitch/` module folder with an `index.ts`.
- **19.** "No se pudo guardar el cambio…" is one `updateErrorText`.
- **20.** `renderTrigger={toggle}` replaces a lambda that only forwarded its argument.
- **24.** The local `enabled` is now `isEnabled`.
- **26.** A `switch-row` class replaces the repeated row utility classes.
- **14 (part).** Removed the narrative comment above `EnabledSwitch`.

**`acb4683` refactor(web): build count labels with one helper**
- **8.** One `ui/count-label.ts` replaces two local copies, and `answers` is built on it.
- **9.** The nested ternaries in JSX became `pollsLine`, `handsLine` and `toggleLabel`. The `FeaturedEffects` skeleton takes its text from the same builders.
- **14 (part).** Removed the narrative comment above `FeaturedQuestions`.

**`58d957e` refactor(web): find the featured session with one helper**
- **10, 23.** One `findFeatured`, which accepts `undefined`, is used by `useFeaturedSession` and the three routes.
- **14 (part).** Removed the narrative comments above `useFeaturedSession` and `railLook`, and rewrapped the long lines in `routes/_app/index.tsx`.

**`af1a155` refactor(web): accept undefined in the optional emptyText and confirmIcon props**
- **13.** `emptyText` and `confirmIcon` are typed `?: T | undefined`, as `fence.md` requires for props callers may omit.

**`6f275af` test(web): name the boolean helper parameters with is**
- **15, 21, 25.** `isOtherFeaturedQuestions`, `isFeatured` (two helpers) and `isWithQuestions`.

## Skipped findings

For each skip: what the reviewer saw and proposed, then why the review left it.

1. **`FeaturedQuestions` repeats `StudentQuestions`** (reuse, altitude).
   - Reviewer: both have the same query, vote sort, skeleton and row renderers and will drift apart. Proposed a shared piece or a limit option on `StudentQuestions`.
   - Skipped: the program design keeps `FeaturedQuestions` as its own component, because `StudentQuestions` shows the whole list unfolded with the form as its header.

2. **`isFeatured` is passed through six poll components** (reuse, simplification).
   - Reviewer: one boolean goes down four levels next to the existing `canActivate`. Proposed folding the two together.
   - Skipped: the brief has `PollStateActions` take `isFeatured` and hide Activar. `canActivate` disables the button instead, so merging them changes the screen.

3. **`useFeaturedSession` and the `select` type parameter in the API layer** (simplification).
   - Reviewer: generic plumbing for one call site. Proposed `.find` inside `ContentTab`.
   - Skipped: the program design chose this hook, a module-level `select`, at your request.

4. **`useUpdateSession` invalidates polls and raised hands on every update** (efficiency).
   - Reviewer: title edits and the featured-questions switch trigger refetches that cannot change anything. Proposed building the invalidation list from the change.
   - Skipped: the brief fixes this invalidation set, and a per-change list would change what the screen refetches.

5. **The core's `Write` type is shaped by Drizzle (`toSQL`)** (wiki-architecture).
   - Reviewer: the adapter's shape leaks into a core port. Proposed a branded opaque type that `packages/database` builds and unwraps.
   - Skipped: it reshapes the port settled in Q2 and needs a cast or wrapper in the adapter. This one is for you to decide.

6. **The tests in `featured.test.ts` depend on their order** (wiki-local-tests).
   - Reviewer: each test starts from the featured session the previous one left. Proposed one file per scenario, or a reset at the start of each test.
   - Skipped: the brief and the test design put featuring in one file, because a D1 holds only one featured session.

7. **The A41 test in `changelog.test.ts` has to run last** (wiki-local-tests).
   - Reviewer: it relies on running last and is kept correct only by a comment. Proposed moving it to `featured.test.ts`.
   - Skipped: the test design places row A41 in `changelog.test.ts`.

8. **`SessionLinks` prop `featured` has no `is`** (naming-booleans).
   - Reviewer: proposed renaming it `isFeatured`.
   - Skipped: the program design (Q3) names the prop `featured`.

9. **`openQuestions({ featured, featuredQuestions })` in `admin-classroom.test.tsx`** (naming-booleans).
   - Reviewer: booleans without `is`, flagged as borderline.
   - Skipped as a false positive: the object is spread into a `Session`, so its keys are the session's field names.

10. **`leavingOf` and `lineOf` should be in their own modules** (user-style).
    - Reviewer: cited the one-function-per-module rule.
    - Skipped: each has one caller in its file, the rule allows high cohesion, and the reviewer itself called keeping them defensible.

11. **The `FeaturedEffects` skeleton should be the real list with example data** (wiki-web).
    - Reviewer: the skeleton is a hand-written list.
    - Skipped: `.skeleton` only paints `skeleton-block` elements, so the real list without them would draw an empty skeleton. That changes how loading looks.

12. **`FeaturedQuestionsSwitch` uses `text-coal` and `border-sand` on the classroom panel** (wiki-web).
    - Reviewer: the panel turns dark in dark mode, where this text cannot be read. Proposed theme colours or a `bg-paper` card.
    - Skipped: either fix changes how the switch looks, and the colours come from the prototype. Dark mode is for you to decide.

13. **The featured-questions switch renders nothing while the session loads** (wiki-web).
    - Reviewer: it appears late and pushes the questions down. Proposed a skeleton.
    - Skipped: a skeleton changes how loading looks.

14. **The admin rail gets `featuredPosition` and searches the list again for the id** (simplification, altitude).
    - Reviewer: the route turns the featured session into a position and the rail turns it back. Proposed passing the session itself.
    - Skipped: the program design (Q3) chose `featuredPosition`.

15. **The not-featured note is placed by two different rules in the polls tab and the panel** (altitude).
    - Reviewer: proposed one rule for both.
    - Skipped: placing it under the last draft is validation fix `ee83edd` (row B39), and a single rule would move the note.

16. **`usePolls({ sessionId: featured?.id ?? "" })` uses an empty string as a placeholder** (simplification).
    - Reviewer: the types accept an id that must never reach the API. Proposed a hook that owns the guard.
    - Skipped: the guard sits in the same call, and a new module for one call site was judged not worth it.

17. **`FeaturedQuestions` wraps only its list in a skeleton, not the whole card** (wiki-web).
    - Reviewer: the rule is to wrap a whole card, never its inside.
    - Skipped: the change alters how the validated card looks while loading.

18. **`FeaturedQuestionsSwitch` repeats the question row's card classes** (wiki-web, low severity).
    - Reviewer: proposed a shared class.
    - Skipped: only `rounded-[14px] border-[1.5px] border-sand` is shared, and the colours fall under skip 12.

## Check and test output

Run in `app/` on the committed HEAD (`6f275af`), with a clean tree:

```
$ tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json
$ oxlint && oxfmt --check .
Checking formatting...
All matched files use the correct format.
Finished in 192ms on 497 files using 16 threads.

@kurasu/api:test:  Test Files  21 passed (21)
@kurasu/api:test:       Tests  225 passed | 1 skipped (226)
@kurasu/web:test:  Test Files  25 passed (25)
@kurasu/web:test:       Tests  285 passed (285)
 Tasks:    2 successful, 2 total
```

The test lines come from turbo's cache, replaying the full uncached run on the same final tree (`/tmp/review-r3-test.log`). The full suite also passed after rounds 1 and 2. The raised-hands API file was run alone once after its fixture change: 9 passed.

## Local leftovers

- **Processes:** none running. All 42 reviewer tabs are closed.
- **`/tmp`:** `review-r1-test.log`, `review-r2-test.log`, `review-r3-test.log`.
- **`app/apps/api/.alchemy/`:** my four `pnpm test` runs and the single raised-hands run added stages:

edits.oldText: ### Open items
edits.newText:
- La review paró en la ronda 3 por el límite del skill, no porque se acabaran los hallazgos (la ronda 3 todavía trajo 9).
- Arreglos de la review, sin cambio de comportamiento: un helper `updateLeaving` para la salida de la destacada; `repositoryOf` devuelve solo `writes`; `polls.isFeatured` sobre `featuredSession`; el fixture de manos ya no siembra la mano de Ana; `SessionRailNode` para los dos caminos; `ui/SwitchButton`, `switch-row`, `updateErrorText` y los colores `blush`/`wine` en los switches; `ui/count-label.ts`; `findFeatured` único; `EnabledSwitch/` como carpeta; props opcionales `?: T | undefined`; parámetros booleanos con `is`.
- Restos de la review: `/tmp/review-r1-test.log`, `review-r2-test.log`, `review-r3-test.log`; `app/apps/api/.alchemy/` del worktree creció a 1,3 GB.

### Open items

Hallazgos que la review saltó (detalle en `reports/review/ledger.md`). Cada uno: aplicarlo o dejarlo.

- **R5 · `Write` del core tiene la forma de Drizzle (`toSQL`).** El revisor de arquitectura ve la forma del adaptador filtrada en un puerto del core y propone un tipo opaco con marca que arma y desarma `packages/database`. Se saltó porque cambia el puerto que se decidió en Q2 y pide un cast o un wrapper en el adaptador. Recomendación: aplicarlo; es el único que toca una regla de la arquitectura (el core no conoce a Drizzle), y el comportamiento no cambia.
- **R12 · `FeaturedQuestionsSwitch` en modo oscuro.** En el panel del aula, que se pone oscuro en modo oscuro, el switch usa `text-coal` y `border-sand` y el texto no se lee. Propone colores del tema o una card `bg-paper`. Se saltó porque cambia cómo se ve el switch y los colores vienen del prototipo. Recomendación: aplicarlo con colores del tema, como el resto del panel.
- **R13 y R17 · Carga sin skeleton.** El switch de preguntas destacadas no dibuja nada mientras carga la sesión y empuja las preguntas hacia abajo al aparecer (R13); `FeaturedQuestions` envuelve en skeleton solo su lista y no la card entera, contra la regla de la wiki `web` (R17). Se saltaron porque cambian cómo se ve la carga. Recomendación: dejarlos, salvo que quieras la regla de la wiki al pie de la letra.
- **R1 · `FeaturedQuestions` repite a `StudentQuestions`** (misma query, orden por votos, skeleton y filas); propone una pieza compartida o un límite en `StudentQuestions`. Se saltó porque el program design los deja separados. Recomendación: dejarlo.
- **R4 · `useUpdateSession` invalida encuestas y manos en cada cambio**, incluso editar el título; propone armar la lista desde el cambio. Se saltó porque el program design fijó ese conjunto. Recomendación: dejarlo; son dos pedidos de más en una pantalla del profe.
- **R6 y R7 · Tests que dependen del orden**: los de `featured.test.ts` arrancan de la destacada que dejó el anterior, y el de A41 en `changelog.test.ts` tiene que correr último. Proponen un archivo por escenario o mover A41 a `featured.test.ts`. Se saltaron porque el test design los ubicó así. Recomendación: mover A41 a `featured.test.ts` (no cambia lo que se prueba) y dejar el resto.
- **R16 · `usePolls({ sessionId: featured?.id ?? "" })`** usa un string vacío de relleno; propone un hook con la guarda. Recomendación: dejarlo.
- **Dejados por una decisión anterior** (recomendación: dejarlos): R2, `isFeatured` baja por seis componentes junto a `canActivate` (unirlos cambia ocultar Activar por deshabilitarlo); R3, `useFeaturedSession` con el `select` (pedido tuyo); R8, la prop `featured` de `SessionLinks` sin `is` (Q3); R14, `featuredPosition` en el camino del admin (Q3); R15, la línea "Solo se activan…" con dos reglas (arreglo B39).
- **Falsos positivos o de bajo valor** (recomendación: dejarlos): R9, las claves `featured` de un objeto que se esparce en `Session`; R10, `leavingOf` y `lineOf` en su propio módulo; R11, el skeleton de `FeaturedEffects` como la lista real; R18, clases de card repetidas en el switch.

# Consistency check: `feat/preguntas-en-la-card` against `d09d518`

Repository: `/home/agus/.herdr/worktrees/agentic-engineering-famaf-extension-course/feat-preguntas-en-la-card` (kurasu in `app/`). Paths below are relative to that root.

Read: `app/docs/README.md`, every note in `app/docs/architecture/` the change touches, `app/docs/prototipos/README.md` and the prototypes, `app/AGENTS.md`, `.mahou/wiki/` (`INDEX.md`, `web.md`, `fence.md`, `architecture.md`, `api.md`, `alchemy/local-tests.md`), and the code in `packages/core`, `packages/database`, `packages/contract`, `apps/api/src`, `apps/web/src` and the test helpers and fixtures the change touched.

## Leftovers

1. **`app/apps/web/src/features/sessions/rail-look.ts:5`**: `export type RailLook = Exclude<RailNodeLook, "locked" | "new">` is exported, but nothing outside the file imports it (`grep RailLook` finds only `rail-look.ts:5` and `:10`). `RailNodeLook` in `RailNode.tsx` is the type that lists the looks, and `SessionRailNode` takes `Exclude<RailNodeLook, "new">`. Fix: drop the `export`, or inline the return type of `railLook`.

2. **`app/packages/database/src/database.ts:9`**: `export interface Statement { toSQL: … }` is the same structural type as the core's `Write` (`packages/core/src/batch.ts:6`). Since the change, `repositoryOf` builds `Write`s and `D1Batch` passes `Write`s to `batch(client, …)`, which is still typed `ReadonlyArray<Statement>`; `repository.ts:41` and `:64` still import and use `Statement`. Two names exist for one shape. Fix: type `batch` and the repository's `Write<R>` with the core's `Write` and delete `Statement`.

## Docs vs code

1. **The featured switch fails silently when no other session is featured.** `app/apps/web/src/features/sessions/FeaturedSwitch.tsx:56-59` featuring a session when `featured == null` calls `update.mutate({ … featured: true })` with no dialog, and `useUpdateSession.ts:32-40` (`toastOf`) returns `undefined` for `{ featured: true }`, so a failed request shows nothing. Docs: `carga-y-acciones-de-la-web.md:85` says "Destacar una sesión … queda[n] en espera, porque pasan por un diálogo … si fallan, el error aparece dentro del diálogo", and `invariantes.md` says "Una acción en espera muestra su error dentro de su formulario o modal". The code has no dialog in this case and no toast either. Fix: give `{ featured: true }` a toast in `toastOf` (the "toast cuando no tiene ninguno de los dos" path of `carga-y-acciones-de-la-web.md`), and change line 85 to say the dialog appears only when another session is featured. The alternative is to always confirm featuring.

2. **Disabling the featured session shows its error twice.** `EnabledSwitch.tsx:47-58` runs `update.mutateAsync({ change: { enabled: false } })` inside `ConfirmAction`, so the dialog shows `updateErrorText`. `toastOf` (`useUpdateSession.ts:38-40`) also returns "No se pudo deshabilitar la sesión." for any `enabled: false` without `featured`, and it does not check whether the session is the featured one, so a toast appears as well. `carga-y-acciones-de-la-web.md:85` and `estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md` ("si fallan, el error aparece dentro del diálogo, que sigue abierto") describe only the in-dialog error. Fix: let the caller turn off the toast for the confirmed path, for example by passing the session's `featured` in `SessionUpdate`, or by moving the toast to the instant caller's `onError`.

3. **`app/docs/architecture/acceso-a-datos.md:76-77`** ("Por qué una sentencia de batch no devuelve filas") says "una sentencia de batch no devuelve nada". In code, `repository.ts:227-229` builds `writes.update` and `writes.updateWhere` with `.returning({ id: table.id })`, and `removing` (`repository.ts:206-211`, used by `writes.remove` and `writes.removeWhere`) uses `.returning()` with every column. These writes now go into `Batch.run` in `Sessions.updateLeaving` (`hands.writes.removeWhere`, `store.writes.update`, `polls.writes.updateWhere`), in addition to the existing material batches. The batch drops the rows (`database.ts:52`, `Effect.asVoid`), so what is true is that *the batch* returns nothing, not that the statement does. This predates the change, but the change makes the core depend on it. Fix: reword the callout to say that `Batch.run` (and `repository.batch`) returns nothing and discards what the statements return.

4. **`app/docs/architecture/modelo-de-datos.md:139`** says "[La mano] Existe hasta que alguien baja la mano, el estudiante o el profe". `Sessions.updateLeaving` (`packages/core/src/sessions/sessions.ts:139`) also removes every hand of a session that stops being featured, as `estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md` and `acceso-a-datos.md` say. Fix: add "o hasta que la sesión deja de ser la destacada (ver [estados de encuestas y sesiones](estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md))". `tiempo-real-del-aula.md:68` ("La mano sigue levantada si el estudiante sale y vuelve, hasta que alguien la baja.") needs the same clause.

5. **Prototypes that still number the sessions.** `app/docs/prototipos/piezas.html:219` draws each rail node with `${i + 1}` and the `live` look for every enabled session. `app/docs/prototipos/marca-cuervo.html:201,211,218` draws a numbered node and the kicker "Sesión 2 de ${SESSIONS.length}". The code draws no number and no "Sesión N de M" (`SessionRailNode.tsx`, `AdminFeatured.tsx`, `FeaturedSession.tsx`), and `estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md` states "Ningún círculo lleva número". These prototypes are linked from `carga-y-acciones-de-la-web.md` and `componentes.md` for other subjects (the shared pieces, the brand), so the session list in them is background. Fix: draw the nodes with the check, star or empty looks and drop the kicker, or add a line to `prototipos/README.md` saying that their session list is not the current one.

## Code vs code

1. **`app/apps/web/test/helpers/session-store.ts:50-58`** mimics the API when a session is featured or disabled: it sets `featured: false` on the session that leaves. It leaves `featuredQuestions` as it was. The API (`Sessions.updateLeaving`, `sessions.ts:134`) writes `{ featured: false, featuredQuestions: false }` to the leaving session. A test that disables, unmarks or replaces a featured session with featured questions on then sees `featuredQuestions: true` on a session that is not featured, a state the API never returns (`modelo-de-datos.md`: "solo la destacada tiene `featured_questions` en verdadero"). Fix: set `featuredQuestions: false` wherever the helper sets `featured: false`.

## Vocabulary

1. **`app/packages/database/src/repository.ts:225` and `:275`**: the comment "A statement reads nothing after its write, so several can go in one D1 batch." sits above `const writes`, and `batch: (statements: ReadonlyArray<Statement>) => …` keeps the old name for its parameter, although the change renamed `statements` to `writes`. Fix: "A write reads nothing after itself…" and `batch: (writes: ReadonlyArray<Write>) => …` (see Leftovers 2).

2. **`app/packages/core/src/hands/hands.ts:15-17`**: "A student raises and lowers their own in an enabled session". `raise` and `lowerOwn` now require `featuredSession` (`hands.ts:62,74`). Fix: "in the featured session".

3. **`app/packages/core/src/questions/questions.ts:82`**: "An open question of an enabled session: what the student can act on." `findOpenQuestion` now checks `featuredSession` (`:91`). Fix: "of the featured session". The service comment at `:35-38` ("The student sees the open questions of enabled sessions … votes at most once each … and deletes only their own") puts reading and writing in one sentence. Reading is still any enabled session, but asking, voting and deleting are now limited to the featured one. Fix: add "and asks, votes and deletes only in the featured session".

4. **`.mahou/wiki/web.md:17`**: "wrap a whole card (the highlighted session, each card of a folding section, …)". The code calls this card the featured session (`FeaturedSession`, `AdminFeatured`), and `HighlightedSession` no longer exists. Fix: "the featured session". The line is not false about skeletons, so the entry needs no other change.

5. **`app/apps/web/test/loading.test.tsx:67-79`**: the variables `highlighted`, `earlier` and `earlierCards` name the featured card and the "Todas las sesiones" section, which the change renamed from the highlighted session and `EarlierSessions`. Fix: `featuredCard`, `allSessions`, `allCards`.

6. **`app/docs/prototipos/inicio-responsive.html:100,297-309,336,452,472,478,508,594,616,712`**: the prototype's state key and helper are `highlighted` / `highlightedIn`, and its comments say "highlighted card" and "highlighted session". `:508` says "Only the highlighted session takes new questions and votes; earlier ones are read-only", but every non-featured session is read-only, including the ones after it (`estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md`: "Cualquier otra sesión de la lista … en ella no se pregunta ni se vota"; `SessionLinks` passes `readOnly={!featured}`). Fix: rename to `featured` / `featuredIn`, and change `:508` to "every other session is read-only".

## Not reported

- `app/apps/web/src/routes/_app/index.tsx:46-47`: the empty-state text "Cuando el profe habilite la primera, aparece acá arriba." could look like a leftover of the "last enabled" rule. The prototype (`inicio-responsive.html:487`) keeps the same text, and the enable modal features the session by default, so this follows a recorded design.
- `app/apps/web/test/fixtures/content.ts:22` `lastFeatured(...)`: it marks the last session of a fixture list as featured, explicitly. It builds data for the new rule and does not rely on the old derived one.
- `app/apps/api/test/unfeatured.test.ts:21,41`: the test names mention "the last enabled one" to check that the old rule no longer applies.
- `app/packages/core/src/announcements/announcements.ts:49`: `const visibleSessions = yield* Sessions` is used only for `featured()`. The name comes from commit `1b2a4e3`, before `d09d518`, and does not describe a student write.
- `app/docs/prototipos/aula-responsive.html:196`: "Sesión 2 de 6" is the text of an example slide, not app UI.
- Remaining `visibleSession` calls (`hands.ts:51`, `questions.ts:100`, `polls.ts:171`, `materials.ts:69`, `sessions.ts:164`) are student reads, which `invariantes.md` allows on any enabled session.
- `.mahou/wiki/architecture.md`, `api.md`, `fence.md`, `alchemy/local-tests.md` and `app/AGENTS.md`: no line is made false by the change. They do not mention `NotFeatured`, `SwitchButton`, `count-label`, `findFeatured`, `switch-row`, `blush`/`wine` or the third type parameter of `useApiQuery`. That information is missing, but nothing there contradicts the code.

content.text:
> [!NOTE] Por qué el cambio de destacada desmarca primero
> Un índice único parcial deja una sola sesión con `featured` en verdadero entre las no borradas. El batch corre sus escrituras en orden, así que desmarca la anterior antes de marcar la nueva y el índice nunca ve dos destacadas. Cuando la sesión que deja de ser la destacada es la misma del pedido, como al sacarle la marca o deshabilitarla, la última escritura cambia una fila ya desmarcada.

> [!TIP] El batch en el store de sesiones, considerado y no elegido
> El store de sesiones podría escribir en las tablas de encuestas y manos dentro de su propio batch, como el de material escribe la posición de la sesión. No se eligió porque el cambio de destacada es una regla del core. El servicio decide qué se cierra y en qué orden, y cada store escribe solo en su tabla.

> [!NOTE] Por qué una sentencia de batch no devuelve filas
> D1 devuelve las filas de un batch tal como están en la tabla, con los nombres de las columnas y las fechas como números, sin pasar por el mapeo que hace el query builder. Para no devolver filas con una forma distinta de la que declara su tipo, una sentencia de batch no devuelve nada. Quien necesita la fila la lee después del batch.

> [!NOTE] Por qué hay type guards en el repositorio
> Sobre una tabla genérica, el query builder no puede tipar las filas que devuelve una escritura. Tampoco puede tipar el cambio de un borrado lógico ni el de un insertar o actualizar. El repositorio les da su tipo con type guards en lugar de aserciones. Los type guards comprueban la forma de lo que llega antes de usarlo: que sea una lista de filas y que las claves del cambio sean columnas de la tabla.
----
La entidad `Question` guarda su texto en `body`, a su autor en `author_id` y si está respondida en `answered`. Se muestra sin autor a todos; al autor la app le marca las suyas. Cada estudiante vota una pregunta a lo sumo una vez, con una `QuestionVote`, y no vota las propias. Un índice único sobre la pregunta y el estudiante impide el segundo voto.

### ✋ Mano levantada

La entidad `RaisedHand` une a un estudiante con una sesión. Cada estudiante tiene a lo sumo una por sesión, y la base lo garantiza con un índice único sobre la sesión y el estudiante. Existe hasta que alguien baja la mano, el estudiante o el profe, así que sigue levantada si el estudiante sale del aula y vuelve (ver [tiempo real del aula](tiempo-real-del-aula.md)).

### 🔔 Novedad
----
> [!NOTE] Por qué la web pide todo al reconectarse
> Mientras la conexión está cortada, la web no recibe avisos. Al pedir todo lo del aula cuando se reconecta, no se pierde nada de lo que cambió mientras tanto. Si llega un aviso mientras ese pedido sigue en curso, la web no tiene que esperar a que el pedido termine: los datos que el aviso le hace pedir ya vienen en ese pedido.

La mano levantada, una fila de `RaisedHand`, y la slide actual, en `current_slide` y `current_step` de la `Session`, viven en D1, no en la conexión, así que no se pierden con un corte ni con un deploy, que reinicia el aula y corta todas las conexiones. La mano sigue levantada si el estudiante sale y vuelve, hasta que alguien la baja.

----
Destacar una sesión, sacarle la marca a la destacada, deshabilitar la destacada y habilitar una sesión desde su modal quedan en espera, porque pasan por un diálogo que confirma qué se cierra: si fallan, el error aparece dentro del diálogo, que sigue abierto (ver [estados de encuestas y sesiones](estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md)).
---
- A mutation's `errorToast` is a function of the input that returns the toast text, or `undefined` for no toast. `useVote` takes `inlineError` from its caller instead of reading the input: the word cloud and the feedback show their error inline, choice and scale votes show a toast. An access error shows no toast; the query client sends the user to the login instead.
- The toast comes from sonner. `<Toaster>` is mounted in `__root`, and `showError(text)` and `showSuccess(text)` in `ui/toast.ts` call `toast.custom` with the shared `ui/Toast`, whose `variant` sets the icon and the role: `error` is an alert with the danger icon, `success` a status with the check. They are plain functions so a hook's `onError` or `onSuccess` can call them. `test/setup.ts` calls `toast.dismiss()` after each test, because sonner keeps its toasts in module state outside the rendered tree and one test's toast would show up in the next.
- Loading: a part that reads data renders `data == null ? <SkeletonOf>…</SkeletonOf> : …`. `ui/SkeletonOf` wraps the real part filled with example data, kept per topic in `features/<topic>/*-examples.ts`, so the skeleton takes the part's own size. Skeletons are coarse: wrap a whole card (the highlighted session, each card of a folding section, each poll card, each list row, the slide, the header's name and avatar), never the inside of one. `.skeleton` paints the wrapped card as one soft grey block in the theme's colours and hides everything inside it, text, buttons and icons included. It adds the `.skeleton` class, `inert` and `aria-hidden`. It adds `aria-hidden` as well as `inert` because Testing Library ignores `inert`, and a screen reader must not read the example data.
- The login check does not block the page. `useMe` is built on `useApiQuery`, and components do the redirects: `_app` renders `<Navigate to="/setup">` for an incomplete profile, and the query client sends the user to the login on an access error.
- A query throws to the error boundary only when it has no data and the error is not an access error (`throwOnError` in `api/create-query-client.ts`); a failed refetch keeps the data already on screen. The router's `defaultErrorComponent` is `ui/ErrorScreen`, whose "Volver al inicio" calls `queryClient.resetQueries` on the queries in error before navigating home. Resetting React Query's error boundary is not enough: the reset lasts only until the first query mounts, so a page reached through a redirect, such as the teacher's `/admin` after `/`, mounts its query still in error and throws again.

**What each fix changed**
1. **Fix 1 and Fix 2 (toast rules).** I removed `toastOf` from `useUpdateSession`. `SessionUpdate` now takes an optional `errorText`, and `errorToast` returns it. The callers that want a toast set it:
   - `FeaturedSwitch`, instant featuring with no other featured session: "No se pudo destacar la sesión."
   - `EnabledSwitch`, instant disable of a non-featured session: "No se pudo deshabilitar la sesión."

   - The dialog paths (enable, confirmed featuring, confirmed disable of the featured session) pass no `errorText`, so they show no toast and keep the error inside the dialog.
2. **Fix 3.** `session-store.ts` now sets `featuredQuestions: false` wherever it sets `featured: false` on the session that leaves.
3. **Fix 4.** `RailLook` is no longer exported.
4. **Fix 5.** `database.ts` no longer has `Statement`. `batch` takes `ReadonlyArray<Write>` from the core, with the parameter named `writes`. In `repository.ts`:
   - The local pending-write type is now `PendingWrite`.
   - The comment above `const writes` now reads "A write reads nothing after itself, so several can go in one D1 batch."
   - The repository's own `batch` parameter is named `pending`, not `writes`, because oxlint's `no-shadow` rule rejects `writes` there. That is the one deviation from your wording.
5. **Fix 6.** The comments in `hands.ts` (raise and lower in the featured session) and `questions.ts` (`findOpenQuestion` is about the featured session; students read questions of enabled sessions and ask, vote and delete only in the featured one) are reworded.

# Implementation status report

`implement` keeps `implementation-status.md` in the change's scratch folder current while subagents work. This skill prompts, spawns and closes no subagent, and writes no file.

## What it reads

`implementation-status.md`, then the conversation, for the last status report given in it, if there is one.

## The report

Start with the blocking questions: each question a subagent is waiting on, with the repository, the subagent's label, what it asked and why it cannot continue without the answer.

Then one section per repository that changed since the last report:

1. **Status.** One or two lines: the stage the repository is in, the commits since the last report, and the subagent or check running on it. With no earlier report in the conversation, give every repository its full status.
2. **Highlights.** What happened in the repository since the last report that the status does not show: a departure from the design, a fact that changed a plan, a crash and the work it lost.
3. **Open items.** Every item in the repository that waits on the user, numbered across the whole report. Give each item the context to decide without asking back: why the item exists (why the reviewer proposed the change, why the subagent raised the flag), what the code does today, why it was skipped or held, and the changes each answer would require. An item the user already settled in the conversation does not appear.

When the same change, highlight or open item applies to several repositories, describe that change, highlight or item once, in a separate section before the repositories, naming the repositories it covers. Each repository's section then gives only what differs for it.

The repositories that did not change since the last report share a single entry after the repository sections: one line naming them, with the stage each one is in. A repository with open items still gets its own section, even if nothing else changed.

Keep the highlights short.

# Implementation status report

`implement` keeps `implementation-status.md` in the change's scratch folder current while subagents work. This skill prompts, spawns and closes no subagent, and writes no file.

## What it reads

`implementation-status.md`, then the conversation, for the last status report given in it, if there is one.

## The report

Start with the blocking questions: each question a subagent is waiting on, with the repository, the subagent's label, what it asked and why it cannot continue without the answer.

Then one section per repository that changed since the last report:

Load mahou:basics first. Then read `.mahou/report.md` if present.

# Report

A report is what the user reads after the work is done: the answer to a question, the findings of an investigation, the summary of a change. This is not the design tree, the annotation loop, or a document going into the project's docs. Those have their own shape.

Load `superpowers:unslop` first, before writing anything. Hold its rules while drafting the report, the same way you hold the rules below. Its agent pass is for documents; there is no pass here. Write clean the first time. When the skill is not installed, say so and continue.

## Lead with the answer

State the answer or the conclusion first. The investigation, the searches, the rounds of questions that produced it come after, as support. A reader who only has time for the first sentence should still walk away knowing the answer.

## Diagram what reads clearer as a picture

A flow across components, a relationship, a structure with several parts reads clearer as a diagram than as prose. Validate every diagram with `superpowers:mermaid` before it is shown; when that skill is not installed, say so and show the diagram unvalidated.

## Separate what is verified from what is claimed

A pitch, a ticket, a doc can assert something the code does not back up. Say which is which. When a verified fact contradicts a claim or a decision already made, say so plainly, in the first sentence, not folded into a paragraph where it reads as one more detail.

## Report only what bears on the ask

An investigation touches more than it needs to report. Cut what does not serve the question asked or the decision at hand.

## Structure by what the reader needs, not by where it came from

When several searches, agents, or rounds feed one report, organize it around the questions they answer, not around which one produced which piece. "Agent 1 found X, agent 2 found Y" tells the reader about the work, not about the answer.

## Name what you refer to

Refer to code, rows, questions and items by their name or by what they do, not by a bare pointer. Write "the delete button in the student editor removes by the sorted index", not ":120"; write "the collision question", not "Q4". A line number, row id or question number on its own makes the reader stop and look it up before the sentence means anything. A reference in the form mahou:basics gives under Referencing code can follow the name as a pointer to the place, but it never stands in for the name.

1. **Approve the docs draft** (`docs-draft-reconcile/draft.md`).

   - **If you approve:** I write it into the branch and commit it.
   - **If you don't:** the docs keep saying the old thing in those places.

2. **Attach this session to the trail.**
   - **Why:** Entire records a session as a checkpoint attached to a commit, and a trail shows the checkpoints of its branch.
   - **The catch:** none of the 21 commits has a checkpoint, because Entire didn't record the subagents' sessions in the herdr worktrees. The step I added to `.mahou/implement.md` assumes there is one.
   - **Option (a):** `entire session attach` on the last commit (`319ada2`, refactor(database)). It rewrites only that commit to add a trailer, which is safe because it isn't pushed.
   - **Option (b):** don't attach this session.
   - **Either way,** the step in `.mahou/implement.md` needs adjusting. It would say to rewrite the last commit before pushing, or it would drop the step.

3. **R5: the core's `Write` type is shaped like Drizzle.**
   - **The finding:** the type that the core's `Batch` port receives is described by Drizzle's `toSQL()`. The architecture reviewer flagged this because the core shouldn't know which query builder the adapter uses.
   - **The proposal:** an opaque branded type that `packages/database` creates and unwraps.
   - **Why it was skipped:** it reshapes the port decided in Q2 and needs a cast or a wrapper in the adapter.
   - **If you apply it:** it touches `core/src/batch.ts`, `database/src/repository.ts` and `database.ts`. Behaviour doesn't change.
   - **Recommendation:** apply it.

4. **R12: the "Preguntas destacadas" switch can't be read in dark mode.**
   - **The finding:** the classroom panel turns dark in dark mode, but the switch uses `text-coal` and `border-sand`, the light-mode colours from the prototype, so its text can't be read.
   - **Why it was skipped:** changing it changes how the switch looks.
   - **If you apply it:** use theme colours, like the rest of the panel. Light mode doesn't change.
   - **Recommendation:** apply it.

5. **R6 and R7: tests that depend on their order.**
   - **The finding:** the tests in `featured.test.ts` start from the featured session the previous test left, and the "featuring creates no changelog item" test in `changelog.test.ts` has to run last. Both break if the order changes.
   - **Why they were skipped:** the test design placed them that way, because a test database holds only one featured session.
   - **Recommendation:** move the changelog test into `featured.test.ts`, which doesn't change what it tests, and leave the order inside `featured.test.ts`. The alternative, one file per scenario, multiplies the files.

6. **R13 and R17: loading with no skeleton.**

Enable Entire with session tracking for your AI agent workflows.

If Entire is not yet configured, this runs the full configuration flow.
If Entire is already configured but disabled, this re-enables it.

Existing git hooks are kept: each is moved to <hook>.pre-entire and runs after
Entire's hook.

If the current directory is not a git repository, Entire can initialize one
for you and create an initial commit. It never creates or pushes to a remote —
publish the repository yourself when you're ready.

Usage:
  entire enable [flags]

Flags:
      --absolute-git-hook-path               Embed full binary path in git hooks (for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles)
      --agent string                         Agent to set up hooks for (e.g., antigravity, claude-code, codex, copilot-cli, cursor, factoryai-droid, opencode, pi; external agents on $PATH are also available). Enables non-interactive mode.
      --agent-help-skill entire agent-help   Install the stable Entire agent-help skill (points agents at entire agent-help) for selected agent(s)
      --checkpoint-backend string            Checkpoint storage backend: refs (default; one git ref per checkpoint) or branch (legacy shared entire/checkpoints/v1 branch)
      --checkpoint-push-remote string        Git remote for checkpoint uploads (saved to .entire/settings.local.json, even with --project)
      --checkpoint-remote string             Checkpoint remote in provider:owner/repo format; providers: github, gitlab (e.g., github:org/checkpoints-repo)
  -f, --force                                Force reinstall hooks (removes existing Entire hooks first)
  -h, --help                                 help for enable
      --import-history                       During first-time setup, import the selected agents' existing session history (last 30 days) without prompting
      --init-repo                            If not a git repo, initialize one non-interactively
      --initial-commit-message string        Commit message for the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --local                                Write settings to .entire/settings.local.json instead of .entire/settings.json
      --no-init-repo                         If not a git repo, exit instead of prompting to initialize one
      --project                              Write settings to .entire/settings.json even if it already exists
      --search-skill                         Install the optional Entire search skill for selected agent(s)
      --skip-initial-commit                  Don't create the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --skip-push-sessions                   Disable automatic pushing of session logs on git push
      --telemetry                            Enable anonymous usage analytics (default true)
  -y, --yes                                  Accept all defaults without prompting (in a non-repo directory: init git and commit; then enable all agents and accept telemetry). In an existing repository it lists the configuration files to commit rather than committing them. Does not import existing agent history — see --import-history

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

attach prints what it is about to do and asks before doing it. Without a
terminal (an agent or a script) it changes nothing and exits non-zero; show
the user what it printed, and once they agree, rerun with --force.

A session can be attached to more than one commit. Each checkpoint records the
turns since the session's previous checkpoint.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

Works with any registered agent, including external agents enabled via
external_agents in .entire/settings.local.json (that file only, and only
when it is untracked). Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.

If --agent doesn't locate a transcript, Entire auto-detects the agent from
the transcript and prints the detected agent name.
